name: Motion Sensor
description: A wireless, battery-powered motion sensor that sends on when it detects motion and off when the motion has stopped.

steps.text: Remove the screw and cover from the battery compartment on the back with a small Phillips screwdriver.
Attach the included 9V battery; leave the cover off for now.
Wait 5 minutes for the circuit to stabilize.
Tap the SET button a couple of times while watching the front of the sensor.
steps.expect: Red LED behind the lens flashes on each tap

steps.text: Secure the swivel mounting bracket with the two included screws.
Slide the Motion Sensor onto the bracket (toward the right) until it clicks, and aim it at the area to watch.
Test by walking through the area.
steps.expect: Responders turn on with motion and off 30 seconds after the last motion (default)

notes: To control powerline-only devices, at least one Access Point 2443 or other dual-band device is needed.

Avoid aiming at mirrors, windows or direct sunlight; avoid air ducts, steam, oil, fireplaces and large obstructions; keep the lens free of dirt, snow and ice; and for pet rejection, keep climbable furniture over 3 ft more than 6 ft from the sensor.

Jumpers set sensitivity (1), LED off (2), night-only (3), on-only (4) and software management (5); after changing one, tap the SET button once, wait 10 seconds and trigger motion. The left dial sets the off countdown (30 seconds to 2 hours) and the right dial sets the day/night threshold.
The Motion Sensor 2842 Quick Start Guide (2014) says to install jumper 5 to configure night-only mode and light sensitivity from the Hub.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button for 5 seconds.
steps.expect: LED behind the lens blinks red

notes: Then turn the responder on (or set it to any state, such as 50% or off) and press and hold its SET button until it double-beeps; the Motion Sensor's LED stops blinking. Test by tapping the Motion Sensor's SET button.
Repeat for each responder; the documents give limits of 30 and of 32 responders.

When adding it to a Hub, the Motion Sensor 2842 Quick Start Guide (2014) says to remove the back cover, press and hold the SET button until the status LED blinks, then tap the SET button (the LED double-blinks).

verification.note: The Motion Sensor 2842 Owner's Manual (published as the owner's manual but a 2012 quick start guide) says the sensor sends ON to up to 30 linked responders in one place and allows up to 32 responders in another. The catalog records no responder limit.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button for 5 seconds.
steps.expect: LED behind the lens blinks red

steps.text: Tap the SET button.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the responder.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: Have the Hub send ID Request; the device answers with its category, subcategory and firmware version.
While the sensor is still awake, have the Hub send Set Operating Flags (extended) with cmd2 0x18 to keep it awake while the link is checked.
Have the Hub send Ping a few times to check the link.
If the LED is still blinking, tap the SET button until it stops.
When done, have the Hub send Set Operating Flags with cmd2 0x19 to let the sensor sleep again.

notes: The device must already be in linking mode when the Hub starts ALL-Linking, since the Hub waits only about 10 seconds. This links the device's group 1 to the Hub; the Hub makes no link to the device.
The stay-awake and sleep commands keep the sensor listening while the Hub checks the link and reads its settings.

verification.note: No document describes this; it's how the device is set up in practice.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button for 5 seconds.
Press and hold the SET button for 5 seconds again.

notes: Then press and hold the responder's SET button until it beeps; the Motion Sensor's LED stops blinking.

steps.text: If possible, remove the Motion Sensor as a controller of all its responders.
Remove the battery.
Wait 15 seconds.
While pressing the SET button, reattach the battery.
steps.expect: LED turns on after about 2 seconds

steps.text: Keep pressing the SET button for 5 seconds, then release it.
steps.expect: LED turns off after about 2 seconds

notes: Responders that were not unlinked keep responding to the Motion Sensor after the reset.

steps.text: Remove the device from every scene, as a controller and as a responder.

verification.note: No document describes this; it's how the device is set up in practice.

steps.text: Remove the device from every scene on the Hub first.
Press and hold the SET button for 5 seconds.
Press and hold the SET button for 5 seconds again.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking for group 0, so it answers as the responder; the device deletes its link to the Hub.
steps.expect: The Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: If the LED is still blinking, tap the SET button until it stops.

notes: The Hub won't remove a device that still belongs to a scene.

verification.note: No document describes this; it's how the device is set up in practice.

notes: HouseLinc also lists its US identity under the 2420M.
Its heartbeat's cmd1, 0x11 to 0x14, gives the battery level from fully charged to almost empty.
